title: hack/ci: set CI_DESIRED_RUNTIME and CI_DESIRED_STORAGE
body:
I was going through the CI setup over the weekend and noticed these two never get set any more. `.cirrus.yml `used to define them, and four tests use them to check the VM is actually running the runtime and storage driver the job asked for - `005-info.bats`, and `info_test.go .`

They only skip when the variable is empty and `CIRRUS_CI` is unset, and under Actions that is always true, so all four have been skipping on every run since the migration. The checks were added in #14912 and #20161 for exactly this kind of drift, which is what made it feel worth fixing.

Storage was easy since the value is already there - it is the same `STORAGE_FS` the script writes into storage.conf. For the runtime I went with crun because `.cirrus.yml` set that globally with a note saying there are no other supported runtimes, and both CI images install it.

I could not run the system tests locally so I have not seen these actually pass, but if crun is wrong for some distro the test I am re-enabling should say so straight away.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?


None

comments.body:
nice work @vtushar06. I was looking at how this integrates with the rest of the CI scripts, and I have a couple of suggestions that might make this a bit more robust:

right now, the PR hardcodes `CI_DESIRED_RUNTIME=crun`, while `crun` is the default, if we ever run matrix jobs that test `runc` in the future (by setting `OCI_RUNTIME=runc`), the test will incorrectly fail. IMO since `OCI_RUNTIME` is already in the `PRESERVE_ENVS` list at the top of `hack/ci/runner.sh`, it might be safer to fallback to it like this:
   ```bash
   CI_DESIRED_RUNTIME="${OCI_RUNTIME:-crun}"
   ```

as you said the tests skip silently because they check for `CIRRUS_CI`. If we're fixing this for GitHub Actions, we should probably update the assertions in `test/system/005-info.bats` and `test/e2e/info_test.go` to check `if [[ -n "$GITHUB_ACTIONS" ]]` instead of `$CIRRUS_CI`. else if `CI_DESIRED_RUNTIME` ever accidentally gets dropped again in the future the test will just go right back to skipping silently instead of failing as intended, no?

what do you think ?

yeah I'll take the `${OCI_RUNTIME:-crun}` fallback as I checked and` test/e2e/common_test.go` already does exactly that, so it keeps things consistent.

and lastly one thing I noticed while looking at it though - I could only find `OCI_RUNTIME` being read by the e2e tests, it runs/help the `--runtime` flag at `common_test.go`. I couldn't find anything in `test/system` reading it, so bats just runs on whatever podman's config default is. So now if someone did set `OCI_RUNTIME=runc `for a matrix leg, e2e would follow it but the system test would still be on crun and assert the wrong thing. 

On the CIRRUS_CI guards, I agree. I left them out to keep the diff small, but that drift protection is the whole reason those checks exist, so I'll switch them to GITHUB_ACTIONS in the same PR. Thanks :)
hi @Luap99, can you have a look at this, all improvements are pushed only need your final check up.
